metadata.title: Secure Network Guest & Unmanaged Access SSPP
metadata.remarks: System Security and Privacy Plan governing guest, BYOD, residence, and other unmanaged device access to institutional network services.

import-profile.remarks: Institutional security, privacy, and acceptable-use baseline.

system-characteristics.system-description: Capability providing constrained, auditable network access for unmanaged devices and non-institutionally managed endpoints, including guests, residents, and BYOD users.

props.name: relies-on-sspp
props.remarks: Guest and unmanaged access inherits network governance and assurance from the Secure Network Platform SSPP.

props.name: relies-on-sspp
props.remarks: All guest and unmanaged access is mediated by Secure Network Gateways.

props.name: relies-on-sspp
props.remarks: Wireless, residence, and guest access operate as logical network extensions and do not extend trust boundaries.

props.name: relies-on-sspp
props.remarks: User authentication and assurance signals are consumed from Secure Identity services where applicable.

props.name: relies-on-sspp
props.remarks: External identity assertions (e.g., eduroam) may be accepted via Secure Identity Federation.

props.name: device-trust
props.remarks: Devices connecting via this SSPP are assumed to be unmanaged and potentially compromised.

props.name: authentication-scope
props.remarks: Authentication applies to users only; device identity or posture is not trusted.

props.name: authorization-scope
props.remarks: Access is limited to internet connectivity and explicitly approved public-facing services.

props.name: lateral-access
props.remarks: Guest and unmanaged access must not allow lateral movement or internal network reachability.

props.name: trust-inheritance
props.remarks: Authentication does not imply trust level, device trust, or authorization beyond defined scope.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Unmanaged and guest access aligns with Zero Trust principles: identity does not equate to trust, and access is explicitly constrained.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Identity-aware networking principles apply even for unmanaged endpoints, with enforced policy boundaries.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Guest, residence, and BYOD access align with SP 800-46 guidance for unmanaged and remote connectivity.

system-implementation.remarks: Guest and unmanaged access is implemented through constrained network segments, controlled gateways, and explicit egress policies. No internal systems or privileged services are directly reachable.

components.title: Guest and Unmanaged Access Segment
components.description: Network segment dedicated to unmanaged and guest devices with restricted connectivity.

components.title: Guest Access Gateway
components.description: Gateway enforcing identity-based admission, segmentation, and egress controls for guest traffic.

roles.title: Network Architecture Authority
roles.remarks: Defines scope, constraints, and approved use cases for guest and unmanaged access.

roles.title: Network Operations
roles.remarks: Operates guest and unmanaged access services in accordance with security constraints.

roles.title: Network Security Monitoring
roles.remarks: Monitors guest and unmanaged access for abuse, misuse, and policy violations.

control-implementation.remarks: Network, identity, monitoring, and resiliency controls are inherited from Secure Network Platform, Gateway, Logical Extension, and Identity SSPPs. This SSPP defines scope and constraints only.
